Cabochon: 2 directions

Make me a font that looks cut from polished gemstones. Start with jade on a dark red cloth: mottled green stone, a glossy bevel, and one small spot of light on each letter. The person showed a picture. I worked from a description of it, not from the image: one lowercase serif `a`, cut from polished jade, on a dark red ground (about `#7A1418`). The stone is a mottled mid green with paler, cloudy patches, like light inside the stone. The letter has a raised, glossy bevel: a thin bright line runs along the upper left edges of each stroke, the lower right edges are darker, and one small bright spot sits on a stroke like the reflection of a lamp. The letter is a high-contrast book serif. - **What is it for?** A word or a short line at a large size: a jeweler's sign, a book cover, a menu heading, a label. Not for running text. (I chose this.) - **What should it feel like?** Precious, polished, elegant. (I chose this, from the picture.) - **What must it not look like?** Chunky toy letters, candy, a plastic button, or ornament that hides the letter. (The request said the letters must stay elegant.) - **Which styles?** One style in each family, with six palettes, one for each stone: Jade, Ruby, Sapphire, Amethyst, Amber, Onyx. A color font has no variable file. (I chose this.)
